The original four phases were independently validated against their task lists and quality gates.\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/implementation-summary.md:71:1. **Lane 1 — Claim-Adjudication Stop Gate Wiring** closed F002 and F007 by adding a universal STOP veto pre-check and a dedicated `claimAdjudicationGate` in the review legal-stop decision tree, plus persisted `claim_adjudication` events, typed packet docs in `.opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/references/state_format.md` §9, and matching `.opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/references/loop_protocol.md` §Step 4a. New REQs: REQ-026, REQ-027.\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/implementation-summary.md:72:2. **Lane 2 — Coverage-Graph Session Isolation** closed F004, F005, F006, and F013 by bumping `deep-loop-graph.sqlite` to v2 with a composite primary key of `(spec_folder, loop_type, session_id, id)` on both `coverage_nodes` and `coverage_edges`, migrating via drop-and-recreate, adding a shared-ID collisions regression to `session-isolation.vitest.ts`, and documenting the typed `graphEvents` payload shape and namespace rules in both state_format references. New REQs: REQ-028, REQ-029.\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/implementation-summary.md:75:5. **Lane 5 — Release-Readiness Reconciliation** closed F013, F014, F015, and F016 by rewriting the phase-008 closeout surfaces, the packet-root completion surfaces below, and the reducer-owned `ACTIVE RISKS` dashboard section so non-P0 release-readiness debt stays visible. New REQ: REQ-034.\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/implementation-summary.md:114:| Closing-audit Lane 1–5 remediation (REQ-026 through REQ-034) | PASS — see `008-further-deep-loop-improvements/implementation-summary.md` §Closing Audit Remediation Notes and `review/review-report.md` |\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:42:      \\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"D3: Is the mutation coverage graph namespace (`loop_type: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"improvement\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"`) properly isolated from the deep-research/deep-review namespaces in the shared SQLite store?\\\\\\\",\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:72:      \\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"D5: Does any loop phase (init / iteration / convergence / synthesis) actively READ from the coverage graph (`coverage-graph-query.ts`, `coverage-graph-convergence.cjs`) to inform decisions, or only WRITE to it?\\\\\\\",\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:90:      \\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"D5: Does the coverage graph's contribution to the 3-signal convergence math exceed its weight, or is it merely nominal?\\\\\\\",\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:301:      \\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"`sk-improve-agent` follows a different path entirely: its resume contract replays a local \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"coverage graph + registry\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\", and `mutation-coverage.cjs` persists an `improvement` JSON graph with `fs`/`path` helpers and `loopType: 'improvement'`, while the agent only consumes an orchestrator-provided summary as advisory context. That means it does not supply the missing shared `deep_loop_graph_*` bridge for research/review convergence (.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:294-300; .opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/scripts/mutation-coverage.cjs:9-10; .opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/scripts/mutation-coverage.cjs:21; .opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/scripts/mutation-coverage.cjs:50-67; .opencode/agents/agent-improver.md:175-177).\\\\\\\",\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:319:      \\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"Both deep-loop convergence contracts still document a reducer-owned in-memory graph bridge that is not present in the live reducer: deep research says \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the reducer builds an in-memory coverage graph\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" when `graphEvents` exist, and deep review says the same for review iterations (.opencode/skills/sk-deep-research/references/convergence.md:1181-1205; .opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/references/convergence.md:658-683).\\\\\\\",\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:711:      \\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"The published deep-research contract says that when `graphEvents` exist, \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the reducer builds an in-memory coverage graph and derives additional signals for the legal-stop gate evaluation,\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" including graph coverage sub-checks (`.opencode/skills/sk-deep-research/references/convergence.md:1181-1205`). The live research reducer does not implement that bridge: its only imports are `fs` and `path`, and its convergence score is taken from `latestIteration.convergenceSignals?.compositeStop` or `latestIteration?.newInfoRatio` rather than any graph helper (`.opencode/skills/sk-deep-research/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:11-13`, `.opencode/skills/sk-deep-research/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:244-249`).\\\\\\\",\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1177:      \\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"The resume contract promises richer recovery than the shipped journal helpers provide. The skill says resume replays the journal, coverage graph, and registry before dispatch, but the journal module only exposes raw-event readback, `getLastIteration()`, and `getSessionResult()`. If an interruption happens before a `session_ended` event is written, `getSessionResult()` returns `{ stopReason: null, sessionOutcome: null }`, so the helper surface itself does not reconstruct candidate, gate, benchmark, or trade-off state (`.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:290-300`, `.opencode/commands/deep/start-agent-improvement-loop.md:332-339`, `.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/scripts/improvement-journal.cjs:148-203`).\\\\\\\",\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1263:      \\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"The published resume contract promises more reconstruction than the shipped recovery helper exposes. Both the command and skill say resume replays the journal, coverage graph, and registry before dispatch, but the only recovery-facing journal helpers return the max iteration number and the terminal `stopReason/sessionOutcome`; there is no helper that rebuilds blocked-stop payloads, trade-off state, benchmark warnings, or lineage context from raw journal events (`.opencode/commands/deep/start-agent-improvement-loop.md:334-339`, `.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:290-295`, `.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/scripts/improvement-journal.cjs:168-203`).\\\\\\\",\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1530:      \\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"The shipped deep-review reducer mirrors the same pattern. `computeConvergenceScore()` reads `latest.convergenceSignals.compositeStop` or falls back to `1 - newFindingsRatio`, and the reducer then publishes only that scalar as `convergenceScore`. No inspected review reducer code reconstructs a coverage graph or invokes graph convergence logic before writing the dashboard/registry (`.opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:360-390`, `.opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:579-583`, `.opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:671-680`).\\\\\\\",\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1551:      \\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"The standalone graph helper does have bounded weight, not runaway influence: `computeGraphConvergence()` builds `graphScore` from fragmentation (0.25), normalized depth (0.25), question coverage (0.30), and source diversity (0.20), then limits the merged result to `blendedScore = compositeStop * 0.6 + graphScore * 0.4`. Inside this helper, the coverage graph cannot contribute more than 40% of the final blended scalar (`.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/scripts/lib/coverage-graph-convergence.cjs:141-205`).\\\\\\\",\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1735:      \\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"A different namespace-isolation weakness does exist on the shared read side for research/review sessions: the convergence handler never accepts `sessionId`, constructs its namespace from only `{ specFolder, loopType }`, and then calls `getStats()` plus `computeSignals()` / `computeMomentum()` without session scoping, so convergence decisions aggregate all sessions sharing the same spec folder and loop type (`.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/convergence.ts:47-52`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/convergence.ts:92-111`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-db.ts:511-545`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-signals.ts:163-220`).\\\\\\\",\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1779:      \\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"The published `sk-improve-agent` contract and visible auto workflow keep that mutation coverage graph local to the improvement runtime rather than bridging it into the shared coverage-graph MCP. The skill describes `scripts/mutation-coverage.cjs` as the reader/writer for the coverage graph and says it uses `loop_type: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"improvement\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"` isolation, while the auto workflow only appends the state ledger and runs `scripts/reduce-state.cjs`; I found no visible `deep_loop_graph_upsert` step on this path (`.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:298-300`, `.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:389-390`, `.opencode/commands/deep/assets/improve_agent-improver_auto.yaml:149-155`).\\\\\\\",\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1801:      \\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"The query surface only partially exposes session isolation. `handleCoverageGraphQuery()` accepts `sessionId` and passes it into `ns`, but the inspected helper queries for coverage gaps, contradictions, and unverified claims read by `spec_folder` and `loop_type` only, ignoring `ns.sessionId`; this means research/review sessions can be co-mingled on read even though improvement-mode entries are blocked from the DB entirely (`.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/query.ts:28-35`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/query.ts:55-58`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-query.ts:63-126`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-query.ts:136-147`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-query.ts:238-277`).\\\\\\\",\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1823:      \\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"The shared SQLite coverage graph does not admit `improvement` loop types at all. The DB layer defines `LoopType = 'research' | 'review'`, constrains valid kinds/relations by those two namespaces, and the schema enforces `CHECK(loop_type IN ('research', 'review'))`; the MCP upsert handler repeats the same validation and rejects any other value (`.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-db.ts:17`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-db.ts:136-146`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-db.ts:152-157`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/upsert.ts:51-53`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/upsert.ts:72-80`).\\\\\\\",\\\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:2121:      \\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"`SKILL.md` says resume replays the journal, coverage graph, and registry before dispatch and that the orchestrator skips mutation types already in the exhausted log, but the visible autonomous loop never invokes `mutation-coverage.cjs` before candidate generation. New REQs: REQ-026, REQ-027.\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/implementation-summary.md:72:2. **Lane 2 — Coverage-Graph Session Isolation** closed F004, F005, F006, and F013 by bumping `deep-loop-graph.sqlite` to v2 with a composite primary key of `(spec_folder, loop_type, session_id, id)` on both `coverage_nodes` and `coverage_edges`, migrating via drop-and-recreate, adding a shared-ID collisions regression to `session-isolation.vitest.ts`, and documenting the typed `graphEvents` payload shape and namespace rules in both state_format references. New REQs: REQ-028, REQ-029.\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/implementation-summary.md:75:5. **Lane 5 — Release-Readiness Reconciliation** closed F013, F014, F015, and F016 by rewriting the phase-008 closeout surfaces, the packet-root completion surfaces below, and the reducer-owned `ACTIVE RISKS` dashboard section so non-P0 release-readiness debt stays visible. New REQ: REQ-034.\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/implementation-summary.md:114:| Closing-audit Lane 1–5 remediation (REQ-026 through REQ-034) | PASS — see `008-further-deep-loop-improvements/implementation-summary.md` §Closing Audit Remediation Notes and `review/review-report.md` |\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:42:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"D3: Is the mutation coverage graph namespace (`loop_type: \\\\\\\"improvement\\\\\\\"`) properly isolated from the deep-research/deep-review namespaces in the shared SQLite store?\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:72:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"D5: Does any loop phase (init / iteration / convergence / synthesis) actively READ from the coverage graph (`coverage-graph-query.ts`, `coverage-graph-convergence.cjs`) to inform decisions, or only WRITE to it?\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:90:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"D5: Does the coverage graph's contribution to the 3-signal convergence math exceed its weight, or is it merely nominal?\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:301:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"`sk-improve-agent` follows a different path entirely: its resume contract replays a local \\\\\\\"coverage graph + registry\\\\\\\", and `mutation-coverage.cjs` persists an `improvement` JSON graph with `fs`/`path` helpers and `loopType: 'improvement'`, while the agent only consumes an orchestrator-provided summary as advisory context. That means it does not supply the missing shared `deep_loop_graph_*` bridge for research/review convergence (.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:294-300; .opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/scripts/mutation-coverage.cjs:9-10; .opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/scripts/mutation-coverage.cjs:21; .opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/scripts/mutation-coverage.cjs:50-67; .opencode/agents/agent-improver.md:175-177).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:319:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"Both deep-loop convergence contracts still document a reducer-owned in-memory graph bridge that is not present in the live reducer: deep research says \\\\\\\"the reducer builds an in-memory coverage graph\\\\\\\" when `graphEvents` exist, and deep review says the same for review iterations (.opencode/skills/sk-deep-research/references/convergence.md:1181-1205; .opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/references/convergence.md:658-683).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:711:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"The published deep-research contract says that when `graphEvents` exist, \\\\\\\"the reducer builds an in-memory coverage graph and derives additional signals for the legal-stop gate evaluation,\\\\\\\" including graph coverage sub-checks (`.opencode/skills/sk-deep-research/references/convergence.md:1181-1205`). The live research reducer does not implement that bridge: its only imports are `fs` and `path`, and its convergence score is taken from `latestIteration.convergenceSignals?.compositeStop` or `latestIteration?.newInfoRatio` rather than any graph helper (`.opencode/skills/sk-deep-research/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:11-13`, `.opencode/skills/sk-deep-research/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:244-249`).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1177:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"The resume contract promises richer recovery than the shipped journal helpers provide. The skill says resume replays the journal, coverage graph, and registry before dispatch, but the journal module only exposes raw-event readback, `getLastIteration()`, and `getSessionResult()`. If an interruption happens before a `session_ended` event is written, `getSessionResult()` returns `{ stopReason: null, sessionOutcome: null }`, so the helper surface itself does not reconstruct candidate, gate, benchmark, or trade-off state (`.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:290-300`, `.opencode/commands/deep/start-agent-improvement-loop.md:332-339`, `.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/scripts/improvement-journal.cjs:148-203`).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1263:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"The published resume contract promises more reconstruction than the shipped recovery helper exposes. Both the command and skill say resume replays the journal, coverage graph, and registry before dispatch, but the only recovery-facing journal helpers return the max iteration number and the terminal `stopReason/sessionOutcome`; there is no helper that rebuilds blocked-stop payloads, trade-off state, benchmark warnings, or lineage context from raw journal events (`.opencode/commands/deep/start-agent-improvement-loop.md:334-339`, `.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:290-295`, `.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/scripts/improvement-journal.cjs:168-203`).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1530:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"The shipped deep-review reducer mirrors the same pattern. `computeConvergenceScore()` reads `latest.convergenceSignals.compositeStop` or falls back to `1 - newFindingsRatio`, and the reducer then publishes only that scalar as `convergenceScore`. No inspected review reducer code reconstructs a coverage graph or invokes graph convergence logic before writing the dashboard/registry (`.opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:360-390`, `.opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:579-583`, `.opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:671-680`).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1551:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"The standalone graph helper does have bounded weight, not runaway influence: `computeGraphConvergence()` builds `graphScore` from fragmentation (0.25), normalized depth (0.25), question coverage (0.30), and source diversity (0.20), then limits the merged result to `blendedScore = compositeStop * 0.6 + graphScore * 0.4`. Inside this helper, the coverage graph cannot contribute more than 40% of the final blended scalar (`.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/scripts/lib/coverage-graph-convergence.cjs:141-205`).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1735:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"A different namespace-isolation weakness does exist on the shared read side for research/review sessions: the convergence handler never accepts `sessionId`, constructs its namespace from only `{ specFolder, loopType }`, and then calls `getStats()` plus `computeSignals()` / `computeMomentum()` without session scoping, so convergence decisions aggregate all sessions sharing the same spec folder and loop type (`.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/convergence.ts:47-52`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/convergence.ts:92-111`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-db.ts:511-545`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-signals.ts:163-220`).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1779:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"The published `sk-improve-agent` contract and visible auto workflow keep that mutation coverage graph local to the improvement runtime rather than bridging it into the shared coverage-graph MCP. The skill describes `scripts/mutation-coverage.cjs` as the reader/writer for the coverage graph and says it uses `loop_type: \\\\\\\"improvement\\\\\\\"` isolation, while the auto workflow only appends the state ledger and runs `scripts/reduce-state.cjs`; I found no visible `deep_loop_graph_upsert` step on this path (`.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:298-300`, `.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:389-390`, `.opencode/commands/deep/assets/improve_agent-improver_auto.yaml:149-155`).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1801:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"The query surface only partially exposes session isolation. `handleCoverageGraphQuery()` accepts `sessionId` and passes it into `ns`, but the inspected helper queries for coverage gaps, contradictions, and unverified claims read by `spec_folder` and `loop_type` only, ignoring `ns.sessionId`; this means research/review sessions can be co-mingled on read even though improvement-mode entries are blocked from the DB entirely (`.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/query.ts:28-35`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/query.ts:55-58`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-query.ts:63-126`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-query.ts:136-147`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-query.ts:238-277`).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1823:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"The shared SQLite coverage graph does not admit `improvement` loop types at all. The DB layer defines `LoopType = 'research' | 'review'`, constrains valid kinds/relations by those two namespaces, and the schema enforces `CHECK(loop_type IN ('research', 'review'))`; the MCP upsert handler repeats the same validation and rejects any other value (`.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-db.ts:17`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-db.ts:136-146`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-db.ts:152-157`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/upsert.ts:51-53`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/upsert.ts:72-80`).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:2121:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"`SKILL.md` says resume replays the journal, coverage graph, and registry before dispatch and that the orchestrator skips mutation types already in the exhausted log, but the visible autonomous loop never invokes `mutation-coverage.cjs` before candidate generation. The shipped loop proceeds from integration scan directly to candidate generation, scoring, benchmarking, ledger append, reducer refresh, and reducer-driven stop check, so coverage state does not visibly steer mutation focus selection. (`.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:294-300`, `.opencode/commands/deep/assets/improve_agent-improver_auto.yaml:137-158`)\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:2513: 10641:  File: [wave-coordination-board.cjs](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/scripts/lib/wave-coordination-board.cjs:96)
10642:  Title: Board transition API exists, but the canonical board still does not advance its own status
10643:  Description: The fix batch added `transitionBoardStatus()`, but `createBoard()` still initializes `status` once and `updateBoard()` never mutates it. In practice the board can keep rendering stale lifecycle state unless another caller explicitly wires the new API in.
10645:  Recommendation: Make board status transitions canonical by routing lifecycle updates through `transitionBoardStatus()` or by deriving board status inside `updateBoard()`.
10647:- `F-024-002`
10650:  File: [wave-lifecycle.cjs](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/scripts/lib/wave-lifecycle.cjs:248), [wave-coordination-board.cjs](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/scripts/lib/wave-coordination-board.cjs:236), [wave-segment-state.cjs](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/scripts/lib/wave-segment-state.cjs:185)
10651:  Title: Merge behavior still diverges across lifecycle, board, and segment-state helpers
10652:  Description: The board now uses the intended 5-key composite dedupe, but lifecycle joining and segment-state merging still apply different keys and conflict rules. The fix removed one hotspot, not the three-way divergence that made the merge contract hard to reason about.
10653:  Evidence: Board merge now keys on `(sessionId,generation,segment,wave,findingId)` at lines 236-243 and 513-533; lifecycle join still uses `buildFindingKey()` based on `sessionId:generation:findingId` at lines 248-329 and 417-424; segment-state merge still falls back to `file:line::title` via `buildMergeKey()` at lines 185-278 and 370-375.
10654:  Recommendation: Define one canonical merge contract and make the lifecycle and segment-state layers consume it instead of maintaining separate dedupe logic.

   151	/**
   152	 * Detect trade-offs between dimensions in trajectory data (REQ-AI-008).
   153	 * A trade-off exists when one dimension improves significantly while another regresses.
   154	 *
   155	 * @param {object[]} trajectoryData - Array of trajectory data points with { scores: { dim: number } }
   156	 * @param {object} [options] - { improvementThreshold?, minDataPoints?, regressionThresholds?: { hard?, soft? } }
   157	 * @returns {object[]|{state: string, dataPoints: number, minRequired: number, reason: string}} Array of detected trade-offs or insufficient-data state
   158	 */

Title: Blocked-stop dashboard rendering calls an undefined helper
Description: The remediation added blocked-stop text to `ACTIVE RISKS`, but the branch now calls `formatBlockedByList(...)` even though that helper is not defined anywhere in the module. Any review packet with a persisted `blocked_stop` event can now crash the reducer during dashboard render.
Evidence: call site at [reduce-state.cjs](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:1073); blocked-stop fixture event at [deep-review-state.jsonl](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/scripts/tests/fixtures/blocked-stop-session/review/deep-review-state.jsonl:5); read-only probe `reduceReviewState('./.opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/scripts/tests/fixtures/blocked-stop-session', { write:false, lenient:true })` throws `ReferenceError: formatBlockedByList is not defined`.
Recommendation: add the missing formatter or inline the list rendering, then cover the blocked-stop fixture path in reducer tests.

Title: Exported momentum helper still computes cross-session deltas
Description: `createSignalSnapshot()` now persists snapshots with a concrete `sessionId`, but the public `computeMomentum(specFolder, loopType)` helper still queries only `spec_folder` and `loop_type`. Direct callers of this exported API can therefore mix snapshots from different sessions after the namespace-isolation fix.

Recommendation: add `sessionId` to the exported helper or remove/deprecate it in favor of the already-scoped handler path.
